history.period: Bamakhepa lived 1837-1911; samadhi shrine modern, rebuilt in the 2023 temple-complex renovation
history.summary: NON-TEMPLE RECORD (keep-or-drop decision needed, like seq 612 Siddheshwar Dhotra samadhi): this row is NOT a temple building - it is the ashram/samadhi of the Tantric saint Bamakhepa (Bamacharan Chattopadhyay, born 22 February 1837 at Atla village, died 18 July 1911 at Tarapith), revered as 'Tarapith Bhairav'. Bamakhepa was an ardent devotee of Goddess Tara: he lived near the Tarapith temple, meditated in the maha smasan (cremation grounds), perfected yoga and Tantric worship under Swami Kailashpati (and Vedagya Mokshadananda), and legend says Tara gave him a vision in her ferocious form. After the temple priests roughed him up for taking food meant for the deity, the Maharani of Natore reportedly dreamed that Tara asked her to feed the saint first - since then he was fed before the deity. His ashram stands on the bank of the Dwarka river close to the Tara temple; a Bamakhyapa samadhi temple was built at the place of his cremation within the temple complex and was rebuilt in 2023 along with the Chandrachur Shiv, Bajrangbali and Maa Shashthi temples. The samadhi mandir and the nearby Panchamundi Asan (where he reportedly attained siddhi) are pilgrimage stops after darshan of Maa Tara.
